# Computer Science Program

![Computer Science Program](/sites/default/files/styles/actualite_full/public/pages/images/2020-09/Computer%20science.jpg?h=2acb40e2&itok=gXSFRfua)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Master | 2 Years - 120 ECTS |
| Course Start | September |
| Language | English |
| Location | Palaiseau Campus |

## Description

The Master of Computer Science is a two-year program designed for students interested in algorithms, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, human-computer interaction, networks, and systems. This selective program draws on IP Paris’s cutting-edge research laboratories and world-class researchers.

This program has a strong focus on research. The first year provides a solid foundation in key areas, while the second year offers the opportunity to specialize in one of several fields.

For students aiming to pursue a PhD after their master’s degree, the program is affiliated with three PhD track programs for early research immersion: one in Computer Science, another in Data & Artificial Intelligence, and one in Quantum Computing (within the PhD Track Quantum Science and Technologies). These PhD track programs offer excellence scholarships and registration fee waivers.

## Tracks

1. **Foundations of computer science, Operations research, Distributed computing, and Quantum computing (FODQ)**

This track focuses on the core components of Computer Science, ranging from theory and mathematics to applied distributed systems and quantum computing. Students have to choose one of the following 2-year majors:

* [Foundations of Computer Science (MPRI)](/en/education/institut-polytechnique-de-paris-masters/computer-science-program/master-year-2-foundations-computer-science)
* [Operational Research (MPRO)](/en/education/institut-polytechnique-de-paris-masters/computer-science-program/master-2-recherche-operationnelle)
* [Parallel and Distributed Systems (PDS)](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/masters/computer-science-program/master-year-2-parallel-and-distributed-systems)
* [Quantum, Mathematics, Computer Science (QMI)](/en/education/masters/computer-science-program/master-year-2-quantum-mathematics-computer-science)

1. **Cybersecurity, Cyberphysical Systems, and Networks (CCSN)**

This track addresses the main components of nowadays IT systems. It equips students with advanced technical skills and theoretical knowledge in securing digital infrastructures,formally designing and verifying intelligent cyber-physical systems, and optimizing modern network architectures. Students have to choose one of the following 2-year majors:

* [Computer Science for Networks (CSN)](/en/education/institut-polytechnique-de-paris-masters/computer-science-program/master-year-2-computer-science-networks)
* [Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS)](/en/education/institut-polytechnique-de-paris-masters/computer-science-program/master-year-2-cyber-physical-systems)
* [Cybersecurity (Cyber)](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/masters/computer-science-program/master-year-2-cybersecurity)

1. **Data, Artificial Intelligence, and Graphics (DAIIG)**

This track focuses on extracting information from data, and managing interactions with humans. These majors provide a balanced skill set, combining analytical rigor with creative problem-solving, for careers in AI research, data engineering, UX/UI design, or interactive media. Students have to choose one of the following 2-year majors:

* [Data and Artificial Intelligence (DataAI)](/en/education/masters/computer-science-program/master-year-2-data-and-artificial-intelligence)
* [Interaction, Graphics and Design (IGD)](/en/education/institut-polytechnique-de-paris-masters/computer-science-program/master-year-2-interaction-graphics-design)

### PhD tracks

* [Computer Science](/en/education/phd-track/computer-science)
* [Data & Artificial Intelligence](/en/education/phd-track/data-artificial-intelligence)
* [Quantum Science and Technologies (QUANTIX)](/en/education/phd-track/phd-track-quantum-science-and-technologies-quantix)

## Objectives

This master's degree aims to enable students to:

* Master fundamental knowledge and tools in computer science before specialization;
* Master recent advanced research in various related domains;
* Apply scientific knowledge and concepts in original and personal research projects.

## General admission prerequisites

#### Academic prerequisites

* Bachelor of Science in Computer Science

#### Language prerequisites

* English (B2)

#### How to apply

Applications can be submitted exclusively online. You will need to provide the following documents:

* Transcript
* Two academic references (added online directly by your referees)
* CV/resume
* Statement of purpose highlighting your research interests and motivation for research

### Fees and scholarships

[Registration fees are available here](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/masters/faqs)

[Find out more about scholarships](/education/bourses)

Please note that fees and scholarships may change for the following year.

## Applications and admission dates

[Admissions page](/en/education/admissions)

## Career opportunities

Upon completing the second year of the Master’s program, graduates will be well-equipped to pursue a PhD. They may also explore a wide range of career opportunities in academic or industrial research laboratories.

The French National Master’s Degree is an internationally recognized degree awarded on behalf of the French State, distinct from non-national institution-specific degrees awarded independently by individual institutions.

### **Application dates via the IP Paris application portal**

* **1st session:** from October 29, 2025 to January 8, 2026
* **2nd session:** from January 9, 2026 to March 26, 2026
* **3rd session\*:** from March 27, 2026 to May 28, 2026

For applications submitted via the national **MonMaster platform of the French Ministry of Higher Education and Research (MESR), applications will be open from February 17, 2026 to March 16, 2026**. For more information about their calendar, please visit their website by [clicking here](https://www.monmaster.gouv.fr/calendrier)

### **Prerequisites**

#### **Academic prerequisites**

* Admission to the **first year of a Master’s degree** is open to candidates holding (or in the process of obtaining) a Bachelor’s degree in the targeted field or a related discipline.
* Admission to the second year of a Master’s degree is reserved for candidates who have completed (or are in the process of completing) a first year of a Master’s degree.

General selection principles apply across all programs:

* **enrollment at a highly ranked university**, based on national rankings and/or the international QS rankings;
* **outstanding academic performance**, assessed according to the standards of the applicant’s home country and institution;
* **demonstrate an excellent academic background**, degree and a personal and professional project aligned with the chosen program.

#### **Language prerequisites**

* Applicants must demonstrate a strong level of English, generally B2 to C1, depending on the program applied for.
* A good level of French is also required for programs taught in French.

### **Application procedure**

Applications are submitted exclusively online and are file-based. Applicants will be required to provide the following documents:

* Degrees and academic transcripts;
* Two academic references (please note that it is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that referees submit their references online);
* Curriculum Vitae (CV);
* Motivation letter;
* Additional specific documents may be required depending on the chosen program.

For further information, please consult the [FAQ](https://www.ip-paris.fr/education/masters/faq) or contact us at [master-admission@ip-paris.fr](mailto:master-admission@ip-paris.fr)

A [PhD Track](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/phd-track) is a 5-year excellence program, with a focus on research. It includes both a Master program with tailored choice of courses and research internships and a PhD program. It certifies both a master’s degree and a PhD degree (420 ECTS).

Please note that you may visit the dedicated [PhD page](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/phd-programs) if you wish to candidate directly to a 3-year PhD program, provided that you have completed a master’s degree.

What is the language used in my Master/PhD Track?

The courses’ language depends on the program you are applying to. You may find out what the language used in your program of choice is directly on the page dedicated to each [Master](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/masters).

Are there language(s) prerequisites to apply?

Language(s) prerequisites depend on the program you are applying to. They are detailed on the page dedicated to each [Master](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/masters).

When will classes begin?

Classes begin in September. The start dates for each program are available in the schedule at the top of this page.

Where are the courses given?

Courses are taking places on Palaiseau or Évry premises, depending on the program. Courses’ localization is mentioned on the page dedicated to each [Master](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/masters).

Who may I contact if I have a question about a specific Master/PhD Track?

Contacts for each program are mentioned on [their respective webpages](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/course-finder). They will answer your questions about the program: courses, program prerequisites, etc.

I wish to consult the studies regulations

You can consult the studies regulations from [this page](https://www.ip-paris.fr/sites/default/files/pages/documents/Masters/2025-2026%20Academic%20Regulations%20IP%20Paris%20Master%20Programs%201.pdf).

## Application process

When can I apply for the courses starting in September?

All information regarding **applications for the first year (M1)** and **second year (M2)** of the Master's programs is available on our [Admissions](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/admissions)page.

For **PhD Track** programs, an **online interview** will be scheduled for candidates who pass the initial selection.

**Please note**: there are **no mid-year intakes** at IP Paris, all courses start in September.

How may I apply?

The applications will be on **two different plateforms according to your profile**:

* [IP-Paris platform](https://candidatures.polytechnique.fr/candidatures-mutualisees/logincandidature/?lang=en&dc=ok&cursus=IPP)
* [MESR Platform](https://www.monmaster.gouv.fr/) (Mon Master)

Before starting your application, **please check which category you fall under on our** [**Admission**](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/admissions) **page**.

**To complete the "Educational Background" section of your application :**

**It is mandatory to convert all grades to a 20-point scale, using a comma as the decimal separator.** If a grade cannot be provided, please input the value **999**.

You must submit the general average for each academic year, along with the semester averages. If the second semester average for the current academic year is not yet available, enter the value **999** in its place.

When listing the **institution(s) you attended over the past three years**, please specify **where you were officially enrolled**, including during a gap year or international exchange.

Can I apply to multiple programs?

Yes, you can apply to **up to 5 programs**.

However, each application is assessed independently. Supporting documents (résumé and supporting statement) must be written specifically for each application.

**Please note**: it is strictly forbidden to apply twice for the same program.

Can I apply twice to the same program?

No, it is strictly forbidden to apply twice for the same program.

What are the diplomas prerequisites to apply to a Master program?

**Admission to Master's Programs: Eligibility Criteria and Application Instructions**

* **If you are completing or have completed a Bachelor's degree (Bac+3 and 180 ECTS) or an international Bachelor’s degree**: You are eligible to apply for admission to the first year of the Master’s program (M1).
* **If you have already obtained a Master’s degree or validated 60 ECTS in a Master’s program (equivalent to 240 ECTS in higher education)**: You may be eligible to apply for the second year of the Master’s program (M2).

**Required Documents:**

* You must provide a document certifying the ECTS credits you have validated during your studies.
* If your academic credits are not based on the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS), you must provide an official document explaining the grading system of your institution to establish their equivalence in ECTS.

**Instructions for completing the "Academic Background" section of your application:**

* **If you have a GPA**: You must convert it to a 20-point scale.
* **If you do not have a GPA**: Enter your annual average on a 20-point scale.
* **Institutions attended**: Indicate the institution or institutions where you were officially enrolled during the past three years, including during a gap year or international mobility.

What are the diplomas prerequisites to apply to a PhD Track program?

**Eligibility Requirements for the PhD Track:**

* A **Bachelor's degree (Bac+3 and 180 ECTS)** or an **international Bachelor's degree** is required to apply for the PhD Track.
* **Direct entry into the second year** of the program may be offered if you already hold a Master’s degree or have completed **60 ECTS in a Master’s program (240 ECTS post-secondary education)**. To request entry into the second year, please indicate this in your statement of purpose.

**Required Documents:**

* You must provide a document certifying the ECTS credits you have earned during your academic program.
* If your academic credits are not based on the European Credit Transfer System (ECTS), you must include an official document explaining your institution's grading system to establish an equivalence in ECTS.

**Instructions for completing the "Academic Background" section of your application:**

* **If you have a GPA**: Convert it to a 20-point scale.
* **If you do not have a GPA**: Indicate your annual average on a 20-point scale.
* **Institutions attended**: List the institution(s) where you were officially enrolled during the past three years, including any gap years or international mobility programs.

What are the required supporting documents?

Please provide the following documents:

* Application form duly completed and verified
* Detailed résumé (PDF)
* A supporting statement written specifically for the program you are applying to, mentioning both personal and professional projects (PDF)
* All your transcripts of records, starting from your 1st year at the university (PDF)
* The last diploma you have received before applying or a certificate recognizing your graduation (certificate of achievement), if you have not received your diploma yet (PDF)
* An ID-size photograph (JPG or JPEG)
* An eventual language test result, depending on the program you are applying to (PDF)
* Other supporting documents may be required, which are mentioned in [the relevant Master/PhD Track program webpage](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/course-finder)
* Two letters of recommendation: you must provide contact information for two referents when you fill the application form. An e-mail will be automatically sent to them so they can fill a recommendation form

**All documents must be provided either in French or in English. If necessary, a sworn translation is mandatory.**

***Beware: an incomplete application file may be automatically rejected.***

I have sent my application, how may I know its progress?

This information is available on the application portal. Once you have filed an application form, you may follow the progress of your application by clicking on the “Application Tracker” button, in front of the name of the program you have applied to.

When will I receive the result of my application?

**For a Master program or PhD Track application**, you will receive an official reply by e-mail up to 2 months after the end of the session you applied to.

**Your application is evaluated by an admissions jury**, which decides whether:

* You are **accepted** in one or several programs,
* One or several of your applications have been **rejected** (the reasons of this rejection are available on your application file),
* Your application has been put in a **waiting list** (your rank in the waiting list will not be specified).

Applicants placed in the waiting list will receive a rejection or an acceptation notification by e-mail.

I have been accepted to one or several program, what should I do?

Once your application has been accepted by the jury, you will receive an e-mail to register to the Institut Polytechnique de Paris.

In the case of multiple admissions, you must make only one choice of program.

Please note: once your registration is submitted to a program, you will automatically be considered withdrawn from the other programs.

Also note that it is crucial to proceed to your registration as soon as possible to benefit from all the advantages and services when you arrive on the campus (student card, education certificate, badge providing access to facilities and to benefit from the collective catering offer…).

One or more of my applications have been rejected. How may I know the reason why?

You can find the reason for the rejection in your personal account on the platform through which you applied.

No additional information will be delivered by e-mail by the Institut Polytechnique de Paris’ administration team.

If you wish to contest the refusal decision, you may send a postal mail explaining why you are contesting the refusal decision. You have up to two months to send said letter. Please forward it to this address:

Graduate School – Pôle Master  
Institut Polytechnique de Paris  
Route de Saclay  
91128 Palaiseau  
France

*Please note that it is unnecessary to send documents already provided in your application form.*

Are there application fees?

Applying to one or several of our Master / PhD Track programs is entirely free. Furthermore, the Institut Polytechnique de Paris will never ask you to send your bank details in order to send an application.

I am an engineer student in one of the 6 schools of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris. How should I apply?

The application file is simplified for engineer students at the Ecole Polytechnique, ENSTA Paris, ENSAE Paris, Télécom Paris, Télécom SudParis or École nationale des ponts et chaussées (ENPC).

When you log in to the application portal for the first time, please use the drop-down menu and select your school, then write down your school e-mail address. This will allow the admission jury to identify your file and may automatically fill some fields in your application.

Recommendation letters are not mandatory to submit your file and have your application accepted. You still have to fill the application file with two referents e-mail address but they are not required to write an actual recommendation letter. The lack of recommendation letters will not be held against you by the application jury.

I am a Master 1 student at the Institut Polytechnique de Paris. How should I apply?

The application file is simplified for Master 1 students at the Institut Polytechnique de Paris applying to a Master 2 diploma from the same program (there are some exceptions, in case of doubt please contact your program referent).

If you have an ENSTA Paris, ENSAE Paris, Télécom Paris, Télécom SudParis or École nationale des ponts et chaussées (ENPC) e-mail address, please use the drop-down menu and select your school, then write down your school e-mail address. This will allow the admission jury to identify your file and may automatically fill some fields in your application.

Recommendation letters are not mandatory to submit your file and have your application accepted. You still have to fill the application file with two referents e-mail address but they are not required to write an actual recommendation letter. The lack of recommendation letters will not be held against you by the application jury.

I have been admitted, what is the procedure for registering?

Congratulations! Proceed with your [registration](https://inscriptions.polytechnique.fr/inscriptions/logincandidature/index.php?cursus=MI) now.

Who may I contact if I have another question about the application process?

If you have additional questions about the application process and have not found an answer in this Q&A, you may contact

For masters : [master-admission@ip-paris.fr](mailto:master-admission@ip-paris.fr).

For PhD Track : [phd-track@ip-paris.fr](mailto:phd-track@ip-paris.fr)

## Cost of studies

**Registration fees for the current year are available at the top of this page. They may vary according to your situation.**

The prices of the master courses indicated on the website are valid for the current academic year and are subject to annual indexation according to the national consumer price index – [article 2 of the Order of August 25, 2020 fixing the registration fees at the Institut Polytechnique de Paris for the preparation of the national master's degree and the doctoral degree](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000042283628).

The amount retained will be the one most favorable to the student, except in the particular case of the master's degree in nuclear engineering.

*Please note:*

* *If you feel that the amount displayed in your registration file does not reflect your situation, please contact master-admission@ip-paris.fr before any payment.*
* *No refund will be made in case of resignation.*

I am a student receiving a scholarship based on social criteria

You don't have to pay anything.

I am an engineering student enrolled in one of the schools of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris

All information regarding registration fees are available at the top of this page.

*Note: the schools of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris are the Ecole Polytechnique, ENSTA Paris, ENSAE Paris, Télécom Paris and Télécom SudParis.*

I am a student receiving a Campus France scholarship

You don't have to pay anything.

I apply to a PhD Track. May I be eligible for a PhD Track scholarship if my application is successful? Do I have to apply to it?

All information regarding registration fees are available at the top of this page.

PhD Track students can also benefit from an excellence scholarship during their master's year(s) and then from a doctoral contract with a monthly salary as part of the PhD.

No additional action is required when you apply for a PhD Track. If your application is successful, your file will automatically be processed by a jury to decide whether or not you are eligible to benefit from a PhD Track scholarship.

If your application is successful and you are eligible for a PhD Track scholarship, the Institut Polytechnique de Paris will contact you.

No PhD Track scholarship application will be evaluated by the admissions team.

I am a student in an institution that has signed a partnership convention with the Institut Polytechnique de Paris.

In application of the partnership conventions, students who have paid registration fees or in lieu thereof in another French or foreign institution may be totally or partially exempted from the payment of fees.

All information regarding registration fees are available at the top of this page.

I am a student of the Master's Degree in Nuclear Engineering

All information regarding registration fees are available at the top of this page.

I am a citizen of the EU/EEA/Switzerland and am not concerned by the above cases

All information regarding registration fees are available at the top of this page.

I am not a citizen of the EU/EEA/Switzerland and am not concerned by the above cases

All information regarding registration fees are available at the top of this page.

If you are concerned by one of the cases below, you pay the same fees as EU/EEA/Switzerland nationals

Please note that the list below is based on the order of April 19, 2019 of the Ministry of Higher Education and Research, which alone is authentic.

* Foreign national residing in France and holder of a residence permit bearing the mention "Residence permit for a family member of a citizen of the Union/EEA/Switzerland";
* A foreign national residing in France and holder of a residence permit or holder of a similar permit issued under an international agreement applicable to the French Republic;
* Tax resident in France or attached to a tax household domiciled in France for at least two years, as of January 1st preceding the start of the academic year for which registration is requested ;
* Beneficiary of refugee status or subsidiary protection or whose father, mother or legal guardian benefits from this status or protection;
* Nationals of Andorra and Canadian students residing in Quebec ;

What are the available scholarships to Institut Polytechnique de Paris’ students?

All scholarships opportunities are presented [here](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/scholarships).

How much does it cost to live in Paris?

A monthly budget of 600-900€ (730-1100$) is necessary to live in Paris, depending on the type of accommodation you plan to live in.

What are the available accommodations near the campus?

Master's students at the Institut Polytechnique de Paris must apply for housing when they register. Allocations will be made according to predefined criteria (international students, scholarship holders, PhD tracks, etc.). As the number of available housing units is limited, students are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.

There also private residence available around the campus.

[More info](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/campus/student-life/accommodation)

## International students

I am a EU citizen, or a citizen from Island, Liechtenstein, Norway or Swiss, do I need a visa?

You do not need a visa to come study in France if you are a citizen from the aforementioned countries or the EU.

I am not a European Union citizen, what do I need to do prior to my departure?

A long-stay student visa (VLS-TS) is mandatory to study in France. You may find all information regarding VLS-TS requests [here](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/international/international-students).

Does the Institut Polytechnique de Paris have a Welcome Desk for international students?

Yes. The **International Students Affairs Office of the Graduate School** serves as the Welcome Desk for international students at IP Paris. You can contact them [here](mailto:internationalstudents@ip-paris.fr) for any questions related to your arrival and installation in France.

From **the end of August until late December**, IP Paris is also actively involved in the **GATE (*****Guichet d’Accueil des Talents Étrangers*****)**, a joint welcome desk service for all institutions of the Saclay scientific cluster. During this back-to-class period, GATE is also available to IP Paris students to assist them with administrative procedures related to their arrival and installation in France.

In addition, you may also reach out to the **International Relations Office** of your home IP Paris member school for further support.

If you haven’t found the answer to your question, our team is always here to help:

* For **Master’s students**: [here](mailto:master-admission@ip-paris.fr)
* For **PhD Track students**: [here](mailto:phd-track@ip-paris.fr)

Do I need to translate my supporting documents to apply?

Yes, both diplomas and transcripts of records must be translated. The embassy of France can carry out a sworn translation of these documents.

Can I apply on the Campus France website?

The Institut Polytechnique de Paris is not connected to the application website of Campus France. Applications submitted on Campus France’s website will not be reviewed by the Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Any application must be carried out from the application website of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, [which you can access from this page](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/admissions).

I have another question related to my arrival in France as an international student

If you have another question related to your status as an international student [please click here](https://www.ip-paris.fr/en/education/international/international-students).

If you did not find an answer to your question, you may contact our team:

## WHY ENROLL IN THIS PROGRAM?

### Asset n° 1

Benefit from intensive exposure to contemporary research in computer science

### Asset n°2

Prepare to pursue a PhD at Institut Polytechnique de Paris

### Asset n°3

Build a successful career in academia or industry R&D

Everyone regularly experiences computer programs being inefficient or crashing. In order to avoid that, it is necessary to properly define and study what it means for a machine to compute something. This 2-years major covers some of the theoretical approaches to computer science addressing this, often based on mathematical tools, with a view towards applications. The topics of the courses include:

The master is research-oriented, with a focus on foundations: it aims at introducing students to contemporary theoretical computer science and most students do a PhD after the master, although it also leads to many possible careers in industry.

This master corresponds to the Parisian [Master of Research in Computer Science (MPRI)](https://mpri-master.ens.fr/), which is run jointly by the following institutions: Université Paris Cité (coordinator), Université PSL (ENS Paris), Université Paris Saclay (ENS Paris-Saclay) and Institut Polytechnique de Paris (École polytechnique, Telecom Paris). The first year takes place mostly at École polytechnique, while the second year takes place mostly at Université Paris Cité.

More information can be obtained on the dedicated websites for [the first year](https://www.enseignement.polytechnique.fr/informatique/3A/MPRI.html) and [the second year](https://mpri-master.ens.fr/).

### Objectives

Students who successfully complete the two-year program will be equipped to:

| Advanced Algorithmics | 36 / 5 / English |
| Computational Logic: from Artificial Intelligence to Zero Bugs | 36 / 5 / English |
| Topological Data Analysis | 36 / 5 / English |
| Introduction to Cryptology | 36 / 5 / English |
| Introduction to Information Theory | 36 / 5 / English |
| Distributed Data Structures, with a Spotlight on Blockchains | 36 / 5 / English |
| Introduction to quantum information and computing | 36 / 5 / English |
| Algebraic Topology | 36 / 5 / English |

|  |  |

| Advanced topics in quantum computation and information | 36 / 5 / English |
| Quantum Diagrams and Programs | 36 / 5 / English |
| Parallel and Distributed Algorithms | 36 / 5 / English |
| Randomization in Computer Science: Games, Networks, Epidemic and Evolutionary Algorithms | 36 / 5 / English |
| Algorithmic Geometry: from Theory to Application | 36 / 5 / English |
| Compilation | 36 / 5 / English |
| Advanced Cryptology | 36 / 5 / English |
| Logical Verification of Hybrid Systems | 36 / 5 / English |
| Foundations in Software Verification | 36 / 5 / English |
| Large scale mathematical optimization | 36 / 5 / English |

Everyone regularly experiences computer programs being inefficient or crashing. In order to avoid that, it is necessary to properly define and study what it means for a machine to compute something. This 2-years major covers some of the theoretical approaches to computer science addressing this, often based on mathematical tools, with a view towards applications. The master is research-oriented, with a focus on foundations: it aims at introducing students to contemporary theoretical computer science and most students do a PhD after the master, although it also leads to many possible careers in industry.

This master corresponds to the Parisian [Master of Research in Computer Science (MPRI)](https://mpri-master.ens.fr/), which is run jointly by the following institutions: Université Paris Cité (coordinator), Université PSL (ENS Paris), Université Paris Saclay (ENS Paris-Saclay) and Institut Polytechnique de Paris (École polytechnique, Telecom Paris). The first year takes place mostly at École polytechnique, while the second year takes place mostly at Université Paris Cité.

More information can be obtained on the dedicated websites for [the first year](https://www.enseignement.polytechnique.fr/informatique/3A/MPRI.html) and [the second year](https://mpri-master.ens.fr/).
